units.caption: Supplementary Fig. 7 | Near-peak returns and sensitivity of window-based lifecycle summaries. a, Within-basin proportions of the 2,340 main-sample cyclones with no near-peak return, one return, or at least two returns, using the first-LMI-anchored definition. b, Complete distributions of anchored near-peak segments and subsequent returns; the initial near-peak segment is not a return. The cyclone-count axis is logarithmic. The sample contains 2,217 cyclones without a return, 114 with one, eight with two and one with three, giving 133 return events in 123 cyclones. c,d, Mean bridge duration and trends in later-near-peak and bridge durations under ten prespecified restrictions. S0 retains the main sample; S1 excludes cyclones with exactly one later near-peak episode lasting 6 h; S2 retains cyclones with no bridge or with two observed tropical endpoints and no status conflict at every bridge interval; S3 omits Freddy (2023); S4–S9 omit WP, EP, SI, NA, SP and NI, respectively. Bars show the existing 95% SID-bootstrap intervals. Trend-cell colours encode duration trends (h per decade), and daggers mark intervals spanning zero. e,f, Distributions of changes in environmental meanF-meanU and meanU-meanR contrasts when each master SID is omitted, expressed in 10−4 reference standard deviations. Colours count omitted-SID results, with a logarithmic colour scale. Variable-specific support is retained.
